Motivation and Context

`ChatHistorySummarizationReducer(use_single_summary=False)` is meant to keep earlier summaries and add a new one on each reduction. That doesn't happen when the chat history starts with a system prompt, which is the common case.

After the first reduction the reducer puts the preserved system message at index 0: `[system, summary1, ...]`. On the next reduction `locate_summarization_boundary(history)` starts at index 0, sees the system message (not a summary) and returns 0. So `keep_existing_summaries` stays empty, `summary1` falls into the range that gets summarized, and the result is `[system, summary2(summary1 + messages), ...]`, exactly what `use_single_summary=True` produces.

### Description

When `use_single_summary=False` and the preserved system message is at index 0, locate the summary boundary after it: `insertion_point = 1 + locate_summarization_boundary(history[1:])`. `keep_existing_summaries` then contains `[system, summary1]`, the old summary is no longer sent to the summarization call, and the existing identity check still prevents the system message from being prepended twice. `use_single_summary=True` (the default) is unchanged, so its `offset_count` passed to `locate_safe_reduction_index` doesn't move.

Test: `test_summarization_keeps_existing_summaries_after_system_message` builds `[system, earlier summary, 6 messages]` with `target_count=2, use_single_summary=False` and checks that the result starts with the same system message and earlier summary objects followed by the new summary, and that the earlier summary is not in the history sent to `get_chat_message_content`. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.
